questions.q: Triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(-2,1)$, $B(4,1)$, and $C(1,7)$. Find the length of the median from $C$ to the midpoint of $AB$.
questions.answer: Midpoint of $AB$: $\left(\dfrac{-2+4}{2},\dfrac{1+1}{2}\right)=(1,1)$. Length of median from $C(1,7)$ to $(1,1)$: $\sqrt{(1-1)^2+(7-1)^2}=\sqrt{0+36}=6$.

sections.heading: Equations of circles from given conditions

questions.q: Find the equation of a circle with a diameter having endpoints $(2,3)$ and $(8,11)$.
questions.answer: Center (midpoint): $\left(\dfrac{2+8}{2},\dfrac{3+11}{2}\right)=(5,7)$. Radius (half the diameter length): diameter $=\sqrt{(8-2)^2+(11-3)^2}=\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}=10$, so radius $=5$. Equation: $(x-5)^2+(y-7)^2=25$.

questions.q: Find the distance from the point $(3,4)$ to the line $3x-4y+5=0$, using $d=\dfrac{|ax_0+by_0+c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$.
Find the equation of the locus of points equidistant from $(2,0)$ and $(-2,0)$.
questions.answer: The locus of points equidistant from two fixed points is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them. Since both points lie on the $x$-axis symmetric about the origin, the perpendicular bisector is the vertical line $x=0$ (the $y$-axis).

sections.heading: Finding the equation of a parabola from three points

questions.q: A parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ passes through $(0,3)$, $(1,6)$, and $(-1,2)$. Find $a$, $b$, and $c$.

This question has two parts. Triangle $PQR$ has $P(0,0)$, $Q(6,0)$, and $R(3,6)$. (a) Find the area of the triangle using the coordinate formula $\text{Area}=\dfrac{1}{2}|x_P(y_Q-y_R)+x_Q(y_R-y_P)+x_R(y_P-y_Q)|$. (b) Verify the area using the base-height formula instead.
questions.answer: (a) Area $=\dfrac{1}{2}|0(0-6)+6(6-0)+3(0-0)|=\dfrac{1}{2}|0+36+0|=18$. (b) Using base $PQ=6$ (along the $x$-axis) and height equal to $R$'s $y$-coordinate, $6$: Area $=\dfrac{1}{2}(6)(6)=18$ ✓, confirming both methods agree.

sections.heading: Finding the equation of a line given a point and a perpendicular condition

questions.q: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment connecting $(2,3)$ and $(8,7)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint: $\left(\dfrac{2+8}{2},\dfrac{3+7}{2}\right)=(5,5)$. Slope of the segment: $\dfrac{7-3}{8-2}=\dfrac{4}{6}=\dfrac{2}{3}$. Perpendicular slope: $-\dfrac{3}{2}$. Equation: $y-5=-\dfrac{3}{2}(x-5)$, so $y=-\dfrac{3}{2}x+\dfrac{15}{2}+5=-\dfrac{3}{2}x+\dfrac{25}{2}$.

sections.heading: Finding the intersection of a line and a parabola

questions.q: Find the points of intersection of $y=x^2-2x-3$ and $y=x-3$.
questions.answer: Set equal: $x^2-2x-3=x-3$, so $x^2-3x=0$, giving $x(x-3)=0$, so $x=0$ or $x=3$. Corresponding $y$-values: for $x=0$, $y=-3$; for $x=3$, $y=0$. Intersection points: $(0,-3)$ and $(3,0)$.

questions.q: This question has three parts. Quadrilateral $WXYZ$ has vertices $W(0,0)$, $X(6,0)$, $Y(8,4)$, $Z(2,4)$. (a) Find the length of each side. (b) Find the slopes of $WX$ and $ZY$, and of $WZ$ and $XY$. (c) Based on parts (a) and (b), classify the quadrilateral as precisely as possible.
questions.answer: (a) $WX=\sqrt{(6-0)^2+0^2}=6$. $XY=\sqrt{(8-6)^2+4^2}=\sqrt{4+16}=\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt{5}$. $YZ=\sqrt{(2-8)^2+0^2}=6$. $ZW=\sqrt{(0-2)^2+(-4)^2}=\sqrt{4+16}=\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt{5}$. (b) Slope of $WX$: $\dfrac{0-0}{6-0}=0$. Slope of $ZY$: $\dfrac{4-4}{8-2}=0$ (parallel, since equal slopes). Slope of $WZ$: $\dfrac{4-0}{2-0}=2$. Slope of $XY$: $\dfrac{4-0}{8-6}=2$ (also parallel, equal slopes). (c) Since both pairs of opposite sides are parallel ($WX\parallel ZY$ and $WZ\parallel XY$) and opposite sides are equal in length ($WX=YZ=6$, $XY=ZW=2\sqrt{5}$), the quadrilateral is a parallelogram.

sections.heading: Finding the equation of a tangent line to a circle

questions.q: Find the equation of the tangent line to the circle $x^2+y^2=25$ at the point $(3,4)$, using the fact that the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at that point.
questions.answer: The radius to $(3,4)$ has slope $\dfrac{4-0}{3-0}=\dfrac{4}{3}$. The tangent line is perpendicular, so its slope is $-\dfrac{3}{4}$. Equation: $y-4=-\dfrac{3}{4}(x-3)$, so $y=-\dfrac{3}{4}x+\dfrac{9}{4}+4=-\dfrac{3}{4}x+\dfrac{25}{4}$.

sections.heading: Finding the vertex and axis of symmetry of a parabola from three points

questions.q: A parabola passes through $(-1,0)$, $(3,0)$, and $(1,-8)$. Find the axis of symmetry and the vertex.
questions.answer: Since the parabola has zeros at $x=-1$ and $x=3$, the axis of symmetry lies midway between them: $x=\dfrac{-1+3}{2}=1$. Since $(1,-8)$ lies exactly on the axis of symmetry $x=1$, this point IS the vertex: $(1,-8)$.

Find the $y$-intercept of the perpendicular bisector of the segment connecting $(-2,-1)$ and $(4,-6)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint: $(1,-7/2)$. Slope of the segment: $-5/6$, so the perpendicular slope is $6/5$. Using $y+7/2=6/5(x-1)$, the $y$-intercept is $-\dfrac{47}{10}$.

questions.q: Find the $y$-intercept of the perpendicular bisector of the segment connecting $(-5,-6)$ and $(0,0)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint: $(-5/2,-3)$. Slope of the segment: $6/5$, so the perpendicular slope is $-5/6$. Using $y+3=-5/6(x+5/2)$, the $y$-intercept is $-\dfrac{61}{12}$.

questions.q: Find the $y$-intercept of the perpendicular bisector of the segment connecting $(8,7)$ and $(6,-5)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint: $(7,1)$. Slope of the segment: $6$, so the perpendicular slope is $-1/6$. Using $y-1=-1/6(x-7)$, the $y$-intercept is $\dfrac{13}{6}$.

questions.q: Find the $y$-intercept of the perpendicular bisector of the segment connecting $(2,-3)$ and $(8,7)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint: $(5,2)$. Slope of the segment: $5/3$, so the perpendicular slope is $-3/5$. Using $y-2=-3/5(x-5)$, the $y$-intercept is $5$.

questions.q: Find the $y$-intercept of the perpendicular bisector of the segment connecting $(-6,0)$ and $(6,-3)$.
questions.answer: Midpoint: $(0,-3/2)$. Slope of the segment: $-1/4$, so the perpendicular slope is $4$. Using $y+3/2=4(x)$, the $y$-intercept is $-\dfrac{3}{2}$.

questions.q: Find the sum of the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points of $y=x^2-12$ and $y=-4x$.
questions.answer: Setting the equations equal: $x^2+4x-12=0$. By Vieta's formulas, the sum of the roots is $-(4)=-4$.

questions.q: Find the sum of the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points of $y=x^2-4$ and $y=-4x+1$.
questions.answer: Setting the equations equal: $x^2+4x-5=0$. By Vieta's formulas, the sum of the roots is $-(4)=-4$.

questions.q: Find the sum of the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points of $y=x^2+2x+21$ and $y=-6x+9$.
questions.answer: Setting the equations equal: $x^2+8x+12=0$. By Vieta's formulas, the sum of the roots is $-(8)=-8$.

questions.q: Find the sum of the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points of $y=x^2+4x-11$ and $y=-x-5$.
questions.answer: Setting the equations equal: $x^2+5x-6=0$. By Vieta's formulas, the sum of the roots is $-(5)=-5$.
